messages:
tess_customer: Hey team — today at ~09:12 UTC our app started getting partial SSE events from the Redwood API. Clients reconnect and then receive overlapping partial chunks (duplicate prefixes) which our UI stitches and shows twice.
alex_support: Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal repro and which SDK/version? Any request IDs from the failing sessions?
tess_customer: Using our edge proxy -> gRPC-gateway -> redwood edge chain. SDK is fetch-based, nothing special. I grabbed a recent request-id: req_0af1c3 (attached logs). Behavior: initial event arrives truncated mid-sentence, client reconnects, then gets continuation that repeats last ~20 tokens and then continues — looks like overlapping KV cache/stream boundary.
alex_support: Thanks. A couple of quick checks: can you try forcing h1 vs h2 to the gateway? Also can you capture raw bytes (curl -v or tcpdump) for one session? If this reproduces we can escalate to runtime.
tess_customer: Quick test: bypassing gRPC-gateway and hitting Redwood edge (h2) directly => clean stream, no dupes. Forcing gateway to use HTTP/1.1 upstream => no dupes. So it seems the gateway translation is implicated.
alex_support: That's telling. Can you share request headers and the gateway config snippet? Especially any chunked encoding / buffering settings.
tess_customer: Gateway config (redacted):
```
proxy_buffering on;
grpc_pass backend:443;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
```
Request headers (sanitized):
```
:method: POST
:scheme: https
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
x-request-id: req_0af1c3
```
alex_support: Seeing transfer-encoding: chunked + gateway buffering might explain boundary merges. eng/infra has seen gateways coalesce small chunks and then sometimes cut mid-SSE frame when reconnects happen.
mike_sre: Looping in SRE — can you collect a pcap of client->gw and gw->redwood for a failing session? Use tcpdump -w and include port 443/80. Also capture logs from the gateway worker that shows flush boundaries.
ingest-bot: Automated note: matched known pattern "midstream-truncate-dup-event" (rule v2). Attaching heuristic link: https://internal/replay/rules/midstream-truncate
alex_support: Also flagging billing_ops — duplicates may have caused double-token accounting for the partial repeats. billing_ops: can you hold any disputed charges for req_0af1c3 while we investigate?
billing_ops: Acknowledged — will flag invoice and freeze auto-charge for that session pending confirmation.
eng_runtime_lead: Thanks for the context. From past incidents, two likely root causes:
1) gRPC gateway performing HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 translation and coalescing frames; when a client reconnects we may replay suffixes and the gateway's chunk framing splits SSE frames incorrectly.
2) Upstream HTTP server (redwood edge) may have been closing the connection before full event flush, causing client reconnect to trigger a resumed stream that re-sends buffered tokens.
eng_runtime_lead: Can you include a minimal curl repro we can run? e.g.
```
# simulate client connecting via h2 then reconnect
curl -v --http2 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST https://gw.example.com/v1/streams -d @prompt.json
# then kill connection mid-stream and reconnect
```
alex_support: Also try toggling `Connection: close` vs `keep-alive` to see if the gateway behaves differently. If disabling chunked encoding on gateway removes the duplication that's a strong indicator.
tess_customer: Will try and capture pcaps. Repro window is still open — can provide live access if needed.
mike_sre: If we can reproduce, we'll collect a three-way trace (client, gw, redwood) and look for mismatched byte offsets. Please add `X-Debug-Mode: 1` header so the edge keeps extra logs for 24h.
eng_runtime_lead: On our side we'll review the HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 translation layer for any bug that can produce repeated buffers on reconnect. Also checking KV cache resume logic to ensure we don't resend overlapping tokens.
alex_support: Next steps: (1) tess to share pcap + gateway logs + exact gateway version. (2) SRE to capture redwood debug logs for req_0af1c3 window (X-Debug-Mode header). (3) eng_runtime to triage translation and cache resume. (4) billing to freeze charges for the session.
tess_customer: Ack. One more weirdness: when we set smaller flush sizes on gateway (flush after 64 bytes) the duplication disappears. Not sure if that's a workaround or pointer.
eng_runtime_lead: That’s useful — suggests coalescing/flush boundary behavior. Temporarily we can recommend the customer set gateway flush to smaller chunks or route direct h2 to edge. We'll work on a long-term fix in the gateway translation layer.
alex_support: I'll keep this thread updated. Thank you all — will post pcaps asap. :thumbsup!
